subject.title: [Bug]: Preflight compaction failure permanently locks Composer into "terminated" state

question: Which fix path should own this issue: a narrowed runtime retryability contract in preflight compaction, or a Gateway/Control UI recovery path for pre-run dispatch errors?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but changing preflight compaction from fail-closed to fail-open affects provider/auth failure surfacing, and the three open PRs implement overlapping variants with different compatibility risks.

options.title: Sponsor narrowed runtime guard
options.body: Use the timeout, true 429, and 5xx skip contract with 400/401/403 and billing-style 429 negative controls, then require real chat proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Prefer UI recovery
options.body: Keep preflight compaction failure policy stricter and instead restore the Composer with an actionable error when the dispatch error is known to originate from preflight compaction.

options.title: Pause until one candidate proves out
options.body: Leave all candidates unmerged until one PR has the owner-approved retryability contract, focused tests, and real behavior proof.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrowed runtime guard
recommendation.body: Use the timeout, true 429, and 5xx skip contract with 400/401/403 and billing-style 429 negative controls, then require real chat proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the prior retryability-boundary feedback and was explicitly asked by the reporter to choose the preferred direction.
